focus: A3 per-plugin port matrix: v1 hook/client/event/PluginInput census across the 16 .opencode/plugins modules mapped to v2 targets, plus lib/ shared-module split feasibility
answeredQuestions: Which plugin shape and API surface loads and behaves correctly on both OpenCode v1 (1.19.x) and v2 (2.0.x), and how do the 16 repo plugins port to it?

label: The dual-entry question is settled by an officially documented shape: ONE module whose default export spreads Plugin.define({id, setup}) and adds an async server() method. V1 >=1.18.29 calls server(), V2 calls setup(); the APIs stay separate and no hooks are translated, so no runtime version detection, second package or build step is needed for the 16 local plugins. Host is 1.19.3, inside the supported window.

Iteration 1's F6 was wrong on four of five rows: the migrate-v1 hook table gives explicit v2 destinations for shell.env (ctx.shell.hook create.before), chat.message (ctx.session.hook prompt), chat.params (context), chat.headers (model.request/http.request), experimental.chat.system.transform (context, edit event.system), experimental.chat.messages.transform (context, edit event.messages) and experimental.session.compacting (compaction). Genuinely irreducible: experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.provider.small_model, experimental.text.complete, the global form of command.execute.before, and $.

Hook census over the 16 plugin modules: event 9/16 (codex-hooks-watchdog:74, opencode-goal:3312, session-cleanup:237, sk-vision:13881, system-completion-sentinel:124, system-deep-loop-guard:63, system-dist-freshness-guard:213, system-skill-advisor:1382, system-spec-gate:178); tool.execute.before 8/16; experimental.chat.system.transform 8/16; tool map 4/16; tool.execute.after 3/16; dispose 2/16; chat.message 1/16; command.execute.before 1/16. ZERO uses of shell.env, chat.params, chat.headers, permission.ask, tool.definition, config, auth, provider, $, or PluginInput.project/worktree/serverUrl/experimental_workspace. The fleet's portable surface is five hook keys and 15 of 16 plugins sit entirely inside it.

The callback-arity change is universal: every v1 hook in the fleet takes (input, output) while v2 hands one mutable event, so even 1:1 hook mappings must be rewritten at the boundary. For the 8 plugins on experimental.chat.system.transform the payload type also changes: v1 output.system is a string[] that plugins push strings into (classifier-injection-screen.js:103-104), v2 event.system holds structured blocks pushed as { type: 'text', text }. This is the highest-volume single edit site in the port.

ctx.location.directory is not a drop-in for ctx.directory: v2 scopes it to the location where the plugin INSTANCE loaded and states it is not the location of every session or event observed. 13 of 16 plugins capture ctx.directory at factory time as a global root for path comparisons (guard allowlists, log paths, spec-folder resolution), so on a multi-location v2 host a plugin can resolve a hook path against one root and compare against another, passing a guard it should fail. Highest risk: system-spec-gate, system-dist-freshness-guard, sk-git-message-gate, sk-git-preflight-advisory, mcp-route-guard.

Shared module-level singletons change meaning from per-load to per-instance across a v2 reload(). ESM keeps one module instance per process on both hosts, but reload() re-registers hooks against surviving state that already holds keys from the previous registration generation, so the first post-reload turn is suppressed as a duplicate. Affected state: pendingBySession (classifier-injection-screen.js) and SHARED_TRANSFORM_DEDUP_STATE in lib/opencode-message-identity.js. Needs an instance/generation namespace or an explicit reset on the setup path.

Three plugins import the v1-only subpath @opencode-ai/plugin/tool (opencode-goal.js:16, system-skill-advisor.js:24, system-speckit-completion.js:28). v2 has no tool() helper and no tool.schema DSL: tools register through the synchronous ctx.tool.transform(editor => editor.add({name, description, input: JSON Schema, execute})) and execute returns structured content. These are the only version-coupled imports in the fleet; their v2 branch must hand-write JSON Schema while v1 keeps tool(). sk-vision vendors its own tool() shim at sk-vision.js:12996 so it avoids the import coupling but stays v1-shaped.

sk-vision.js is a symlink (.opencode/plugins/sk-vision.js -> ../skills/sk-vision/vision-runtime/dist/plugin.js) to a 13,911-line bundle with vendored valibot/zod, so it is the only plugin that cannot be ported in place: a dual-compat change must land in vision-runtime source and be rebuilt. The symlink also escaped iteration 1's -type f scan, a hazard for any version-aware inventory script. It is the sole user of command.execute.before (:13880) and chat.message (:13896), and calls client.tui.showToast (:13865) which has no ctx domain in the migrate-v1 table (TUI is deferred to /build/plugins/cli, still unread).

classifier-injection-screen fails differently on v2 through three independent modes, all hidden inside its own fail-open catch (:105): (1) output.system.push(...pending) at :104 pushes raw strings into v2's structured block array; (2) its blanket catch turns any resulting type error into silently discarded advisories, converting the v1 design intent (never affect the observed fetch) into never telling anyone; (3) sessionIdOf at :40 probes sessionID/sessionId/session.id/properties.sessionID, none of which is the v2 execute.after or context event shape, so advisories collapse to UNKNOWN_SESSION and the single-buffered-session adoption heuristic at :88 only fires when exactly one session holds a buffer. The 15 other plugins fail visibly on v2; this one degrades with zero observable signal and cannot be caught by a buffer-asserting test.

Shared-module split is feasible for 15 of 16 plugins and matches existing repo idiom. lib/skill-advisor-render.js (136 L) is pure rendering with no ctx and is reusable unchanged on both hosts; lib/opencode-message-identity.js (464 L) has a shape-agnostic dedup state machine but its key derivation (sessionValueFrom/messageValueFrom/ordinalValueFrom at :63) reads v1 input shapes and needs a v2 event adapter. Two plugins already take their core from an external module and re-export it for tests (sentinelCore, dispatchAuditCore), so 'pure core module + one entry file exporting both setup and server' is the repo's existing pattern. Only sk-vision resists the split because it is a bundle.

__test hung off the default export is a v2 hazard: classifier-injection-screen.js:117 and system-completion-sentinel.js:171 attach .__test to the exported function because a stray named export makes OpenCode load every export as its own plugin under v1. Under the dual object __test becomes an unknown top-level key beside id/setup/server, and the v2 loader's tolerance for extra keys on a plugin definition is unverified. Mitigation: move the test surface into the extracted core module or gate it behind a test-only env var.

The repo declares zero plugins in config: neither plugin nor plugins appears in opencode.json or .opencode/opencode.json, all 16 modules load by directory discovery, and v2 discovers local plugins from both .opencode/plugin/ and .opencode/plugins/. Iteration 1's F4 config-key divergence is therefore moot for this fleet (no config key needed on either host); it only matters for plugins installed into other projects via cli-opencode, where the documented migration is the tuple-to-object rewrite. @opencode-ai/plugin is pinned at 1.18.34 against a v1 head of 1.19.3 and the installed host is 1.19.3.

No module in .opencode/plugins/ depends on shell.env, chat.params, chat.headers, permission.ask, tool.definition, config, auth, provider, the $ Bun shell, or PluginInput.project/worktree/serverUrl/experimental_workspace; the whole fleet's v1 surface is five hook keys plus ctx.directory and (in 5 files) ctx.client. Any dual-compat design that spends effort on the irreducible experimental/$. gaps is solving a problem this repo does not have.

Under the documented dual-entry shape the v1 hook bodies need no version detection and no changes beyond the export wrapper; only the new v2 setup() branch is version-specific. Any proposal that feature-detects the host inside a hook body contradicts the documented contract and adds a failure path the doc does not require.

direction: A single callable default export that is both the v1 factory and carries id/setup (function with properties) as the dual-compat mechanism
reason: The migrate-v1 doc specifies the supported multi-version shape as an object literal: spread Plugin.define({id, setup}) and add async server(). A callable carrying setup is undocumented and unverified on the v2 loader, so it would be a guess where a first-party pattern exists.

direction: Type-checking the port against the dist/v2 preview bundled in @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34
reason: Iteration 1 F3 plus this iteration's doc read show the preview's PluginContext exposes nine members while the real 2.0.32 surface includes session/tool/shell/event/permission/location/storage domains and the hook() registration form the doc relies on. Building against the preview would omit the majority of the target API.

direction: Rewriting 15 of 16 plugins into a two-file (v1/v2) split because the callable contracts differ
reason: The official spread pattern keeps one module per plugin: v1 keeps its existing server() body verbatim, v2 adds setup(). A split would double the load surface and break the repo's flat directory-discovery model, which loads every module it finds.
